text:
Carter Verhaeghe has 10 goals and 20 points in 22 games, and this is a player who keeps finding his way into big moments with Florida, where he has won two of his three Stanley Cups. The production is real; the rate probably isn't.

He has 10 goals on 7.8 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 21.3% when our range for him tops out around 17%. Florida has also scored 11.0 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which is padding his 20 points. On-ice luck like that fades. At five-on-five the Panthers get about 51% of the expected goals with him out there, roughly what they get without him.

The underlying game is still good. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 72% of his exits leaving the zone with possession last season and 9.7 primary shot assists per 60, 93rd percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had him facing competition in the 94th percentile while still driving play at the 85th. He had three assists against Detroit last week. Watch his shooting percentage drift back toward normal; his chance creation should keep him useful when it does.
headline: Verhaeghe's goals are outrunning his chances
